Subject: Hosted API latency onboarding — proposed phased commitments

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is an initial SLO proposal and a simple evidence cadence worksheet for the PulseHealth onboarding (pulse_latency_workbook.xlsx). High level: we want to offer a phased p50/p95 commitment for the hosted API so you can validate in production without locking into a long-term aggressive SLA immediately.

Proposal (summary)
- Phase 1 (pilot, 30 days): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 600ms, measurement: rolling 30-day window; daily aggregation; regional breakdown (US-East/US-West).
- Phase 2 (post-pilot, months 2–3): p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 450ms, add additional observability (per-route dashboards) and a 14-day evidence review for any deviations.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance, provider peering incidents, and defined holiday surge carveouts (we propose a 48‑hour transient carveout once per quarter).

What I need from you to move the draft to legal:
1) Confirm the regional scope (US-only vs global).
2) Accept the phased cadence above or propose adjusted p50/p95 targets.
3) If you want tighter measurement windows (e.g., rolling 7-day), note that in reply — that will change the evidence cadence.

Next steps: if this looks good I will: 1) drop the draft into PulseHealth folder on Drive, 2) open a HubSpot deal activity (PH-4721) to track approvals, and 3) share a final PDF for you and contracts.

Attachments: pulse_latency_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet) — short workbook with suggested sampling buckets and evidence cadence.

Best,

Thanks Rafael — quick clarifying questions before I pass to procurement and legal: 

- Are the p50/p95 numbers measured across all endpoints combined or per-route? We need per-route baselines for our interactive flows vs batch inference.
- For the 30-day rolling window: do you use continuous rolling quantiles (per-minute sampling) or daily buckets aggregated into the 30-day window?
- Can you confirm the fallback behavior if we see >3 consecutive days of p95 breaches in Phase 1? We need an automatic mitigation play (fall back to a slightly cheaper model variant or routing to dedicated capacity).

Also, procurement asked whether evidence will be delivered as CSV export (timestamped samples) or a snapshot report. CSV is preferred for our audits.

If you can answer the three bullets above I will push to contracts and loop in legal.

FYI — forwarding Sara's clarifying questions (below). We should align on a clean, legal-ready answer. My suggested responses are inline: 

[Forwarded message]
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency onboarding — proposed phased commitments

> - Are the p50/p95 numbers measured across all endpoints combined or per-route? We need per-route baselines for our interactive flows vs batch inference.

REPLY: We can commit per-route p50/p95 for up to 5 named routes in Phase 1 (interactive, chat, embeddings, batch-index, rerank). For unnamed routes we default to aggregate account-level targets. If PulseHealth wants more than 5 per-route commitments we should surface that as a pricing/operational add-on.

> - For the 30-day rolling window: do you use continuous rolling quantiles (per-minute sampling) or daily buckets aggregated into the 30-day window?

REPLY: We sample per-request latency and compute rolling quantiles using minute-level buckets; final reporting is provided as both a CSV of timestamped samples and a daily-aggregate snapshot for audit. That should satisfy their CSV ask.

> - Can you confirm the fallback behavior if we see >3 consecutive days of p95 breaches in Phase 1? We need an automatic mitigation play (fall back to a slightly cheaper model variant or routing to dedicated capacity).

REPLY: Our recommended playbook: 1) automatic routing to a compatible model variant in a secondary region (if applicable) for a transient 60‑minute mitigation; 2) open an incident and initiate canary rollback to the last-known-good model config; 3) if the event persists beyond 72 hours we offer a joint remediation review and limited temporary credit (formula in workbook). We'll capture the exact time windows in the SLA addendum.

Action items for legal/discount approval: we may need authorization to offer the Phase 1 per-route commit for up to 5 routes without additional fee and to include the 72-hour joint remediation credit cap. Is that acceptable?

Rafael

Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment below, here is a concise plan we can put in front of contracts: 

Agreed onboarding plan (final)
- Scope: US regions only for Phase 1 (option to expand to EU in Phase 2).
- Routes: Per-route commitments for up to 5 named routes (interactive, chat, embeddings, batch-index, rerank).
- Phase 1 (30 days pilot): p50 <= 120ms per route, p95 <= 600ms per route; measurement: minute-level sampling, rolling 30-day quantiles; CSV export of raw samples provided daily.
- Phase 2 (months 2–3): p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 450ms per route; additional per-route dashboards and 14-day review window for evidence of regressions.
- Mitigation & credit: automatic routing to compatible variant for 60 minutes on transient events; incident review and, if breach persists >72 hours, joint remediation and pro-rated credit per the workbook formula.
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows (advertised 72 hours in advance), third-party network outages (peering providers), and one quarterly temporary surge carveout (48 hours).

Attachments included: redwood-slo-draft-v1.pdf (clean SLA language) and evidence-schedule.csv (daily CSV export template). I uploaded the draft to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cS_example and created the HubSpot activity PH-4721.

If PulseHealth legal is good with that language we will convert redwood-slo-draft-v1.pdf to a contracts-ready addendum and send to DocuSign.

Next steps: Sara, can you confirm by end of week whether legal wants any additional carveouts? If not, I'll route the PDF to contracts and loop in Lauren for any commercial concessions.
